technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the capabilities framework as three independent capability maps: channel, application, and orderer. Orderers validate channel plus orderer capabilities; peers validate channel plus application capabilities.
Represent capabilities as string-keyed maps in channel configuration and expose component-specific capability interfaces so consuming code does not contain version-specific logic.

Use the existing V1.1 capability as the compatibility switch for all identified non-deterministic behavior changes, with unsupported required capabilities causing the participating binary to fail fast.
Enforce the initial upgrade safety rule that orderer capabilities must be enabled before application capabilities can be enabled.

Implement read-your-writes as an optional chaincode stub API that reads the transaction's current write set before falling back to committed state, without changing the default behavior of existing state-retrieval APIs.
Construct channel configuration through public interfaces and builders rather than requiring callers to invoke configtxgen.
Replace package-level chaincode singletons with explicit dependency instances passed through constructors or test fixtures.
Generate peer and orderer configuration files from the World configuration using deterministic templates and explicit value mapping.
Expose lifecycle validation parameters through a dedicated interface, including automatically generated majority endorsement policy information for the +lifecycle namespace.
Use repeatable benchmark workloads and recorded environment metadata for CouchDB query performance measurements.
Treat implementation, unit tests, integration tests, regression tests, documentation, and example artifacts as part of the increment.
assumptions: All eight user stories U1 through U8 are in scope for one increment and must be implemented, tested, and documented.
The existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase, protobuf definitions, ledger APIs, chaincode shim APIs, configuration structures, and test infrastructure are available and buildable.
The implementation targets the Fabric version family implied by the specification, including the V1.1 capability behavior; migration support for later versions is not required.
Backward compatibility is required for existing configurations and APIs unless a user story explicitly introduces a new opt-in behavior.
A single developer performs analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, benchmarking, and packaging; the estimates are work-hours and exclude elapsed waiting time.
No major redesign of consensus, MSP, CouchDB, or the chaincode lifecycle beyond the behaviors explicitly described is required.
For U3, the requested video and presentation image are treated as deliverable technical artifacts; professional video production, narration, translation, and video hosting are excluded.
For U4, a representative local or provisioned CouchDB test environment can be used and infrastructure procurement, large-scale production load testing, and long-term monitoring are excluded.
For U5, callers need supported programmatic configuration construction APIs, but complete replacement of every configtxgen command-line feature is not required.
For U6, singleton removal is limited to the chaincode-related singletons encountered by the lifecycle prerequisite and their directly affected tests and call sites.
For U7, the World configuration already contains or can be extended with the values needed to generate peer and orderer configuration files.

For U8, the existing lifecycle implementation provides the primary integration point and the automatically generated policy is a majority-of-organizations signature policy; evaluating arbitrary channel configuration policies is deferred.
Normal code review, local build troubleshooting, and regression correction are included in the activity estimates, but external stakeholder review cycles are excluded.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing Fabric architecture and relevant packages, map each user story to implementation points, define interfaces and compatibility boundaries, and produce an implementation and test plan.
Add the channel, application, and orderer capability representations and component-specific interfaces, including V1.1 capability constants and supported-capability checks.

Integrate capability maps into channel configuration structures, parsing, validation, default handling, and configuration serialization while preserving compatibility with configurations that omit capabilities.

Connect capability decisions to orderer and peer validation paths, implement fail-fast behavior for unsupported required capabilities, and enforce orderer-before-application capability activation for the initial upgrade.
Create unit, configuration, orderer, peer, mixed-version, and upgrade-order tests, and document how new incompatible behavior is associated with a capability.
Extend the chaincode stub API with an optional transaction-state retrieval operation and define its behavior, error handling, and compatibility with the existing GetState API.

Implement retrieval from the active transaction write set with committed-state fallback as appropriate, connect the behavior through peer and chaincode execution paths, and handle missing and deleted keys.
Add shim, peer, transaction, deletion, repeated-write, and backward-compatibility tests and document usage for chaincode developers.

Validate the non-disruptive organization onboarding procedure, create a concise architecture/process image, record and edit a walkthrough video, and provide accompanying written operational steps and prerequisites.

activities.activity_name: CouchDB query benchmark design and harness
activities.activity_description: Define representative query workloads, datasets, measurement criteria, repeatability controls, and implement scripts or tests to measure query latency and throughput against CouchDB-backed state.
Run the benchmark scenarios, capture environment and configuration details, analyze results, identify relevant performance tradeoffs, and produce a performance report.
Design the public configuration construction model, including the MSPConfig interface, ownership and validation rules, and compatibility with existing configtxgen-generated structures.
Implement the MSPConfig abstraction and supporting builders or constructors for channel configuration blocks outside configtxgen, including conversion to the required protobuf forms.
Integrate programmatically constructed configurations with validation, serialization, update processing, and existing configuration consumers; add positive, invalid-input, and compatibility tests.

activities.activity_name: Chaincode singleton inventory and refactoring design
activities.activity_description: Identify chaincode-related global singletons, document their dependencies and lifecycle, and define explicit ownership and dependency-injection replacement points.
Refactor production code and direct callers to use instance-scoped dependencies, remove singleton initialization and reset behavior, and update lifecycle and execution paths.
Update existing tests and fixtures, add isolation and parallel-execution coverage, and verify that lifecycle and chaincode execution behavior remains unchanged after refactoring.
Define mappings from World configuration values to peer core.yaml and orderer.yaml fields, including defaults, precedence, and generated-file layout.
Implement deterministic generation of peer and orderer configuration files from World configuration values, with template or structured serialization support and useful validation errors.
Add fixture-based tests for generated peer and orderer files, default and override behavior, invalid values, reproducibility, and integration with the existing test setup.
Define the validation-parameter interface and determine how lifecycle namespaces, chaincode identifiers, versions, and validation metadata are represented and consumed.
Implement lifecycle lookup and return of validation parameters for chaincodes, integrate the interface with transaction validation, and support the special +lifecycle validation path.
Generate the signature policy requiring a majority of channel organizations to endorse lifecycle operations, encode it in the validation information, and handle organization membership edge cases.
Add unit and integration coverage for ordinary chaincodes, +lifecycle, policy changes, missing metadata, malformed metadata, and majority-policy calculations, with developer documentation.

activities.activity_name: Cross-feature integration, CI, and final documentation
activities.activity_description: Run full builds and regression suites, resolve cross-feature defects, add or update CI coverage, consolidate administrator and developer documentation, and package the completed increment.
